text:
Ana K: Heads-up — EU dedicated pool eu-dedicated-3 is showing a sustained p99 latency increase starting ~20:07 UTC. Throughput down ~30%, KV eviction rate up. SLA alert fired. Anyone able to triage?

Nina (oncall): I'm on it, pulling console + logs. Seeing a bunch of placement warnings and some pods reporting OOM on the GPU containers.

SRE Bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool/eu-3 p99=1200ms (SLA=500ms), error_rate=0.4%, evictions=182 in last 15m.

Mike R: Reproducible from profiling: kernel-selection fallback counts jumped at 20:05. Primary optimized kernel failed selection due to insufficient contiguous memory, runtime switched to generic_kernel_v1 which is ~3x slower on long sequences.

Tariq S: Any recent kernel or scheduling changes deployed to eu region?

DevEx Lina: We rolled kernel-policy change earlier today to prefer fused-attn for small-seq workloads — might be related. Change id: devex/kernel-pref-2026-03-18-09

Mike R: That change shouldn't cause fallback unless node memory layout changed. Looking at node placement, I see many workloads pinned to specific GPUs due to an older quota rule:

```
# faulty quota config snippet
reserved_capacity:
  eu-dedicated-3:
    guaranteed_gpus: 0.8
    soft_share: 0.2
    placement_affinity: "tenant:high-priority"
```

This mis-set guaranteed_gpus>1 for a subset of tenants caused tight packing.

Nina (oncall): There's a noisy-tenant "acme-sim" that spiked traffic around 20:00. Their batch size increased a lot, and KV cache hit-rate dropped from 88% -> 41%. Evictions spiked, causing more cache misses and larger KV loads.

Ana K: So likely a compound: quota/placement packing + noisy tenant causing memory fragmentation -> kernel fallback. Any evidence of kernel fallback correlating with KV eviction?

Mike R: Yes: timeline from profiler:
- 19:58 traffic spike from acme-sim
- 20:03 KV cache miss rate climbs -> more KV loads -> GPU memory transient pressure
- 20:05 KernelSelector logs show increased fallback events (generic_kernel_v1 chosen)
- 20:07 p99 spike observed

Tariq S: Interesting — batching heuristics also shifted. The batching windows extended because many requests queued on same slot (hot slot), causing bigger batches across long sequences which worsen kernel performance on generic path.

Infra Bot: Node placements: 6 nodes in eu-3 at 90-100% GPU allocation, 4 nodes at >1.1x nominal packing.

DevEx Lina: Quick remediation options:
- throttle acme-sim or move them to a separate pool (short term)
- roll back kernel-policy change (if we think that widened selection path)
- patch quota to avoid >1.0 guaranteed packing
- evict some low-priority placements to reduce fragmentation

Nina (oncall): I'm going to isolate acme-sim to a temporary burst pool and bump their placement affinity to avoid collocating with latency-sensitive tenants. Doing now.

Mike R: I'll revert the kernel-policy tweak to ensure we don't prefer fused paths that force memory layouts that fragment. Rolling back in 5m.

Tariq S: I'll adjust batching heuristic to cap window at 60ms for dedicated pools while we stabilize, to avoid oversized batches creating long seq slowdowns.

Ana K: Good. Also we should patch the quota config to prevent guaranteed_gpus > 1 for soft-share tenants. Nina, can you open an ops change ticket for the quota fix?

Nina (oncall): Yep, filing CHG-6841 and will attach profiler logs + node allocation snapshot.

Infra Bot: Action completed: moved acme-sim -> eu-burst-temp-1. Kernel-policy rollback started (change devex/kernel-pref-2026-03-18-09 -> rolled back).

SRE Bot: Notice: p99 fell from 1200ms -> 480ms within 6 minutes after isolation and rollback. Throughput recovering to ~95% of baseline.

DevEx Lina: Follow-ups:
- postmortem to include: kernel selector robustness, quota validation at deploy-time, KV cache eviction backpressure tuning, batching cap safe-guard.
- propose a routing policy to detect noisy tenants and automatically isolate them before fragmentation.

Mike R: I'll attach heap/profiler dumps to the postmortem. Quick profiling summary: fallback_slow_count=237 -> primary_kernel_ok after node defrag.

Ana K: Thanks everyone. I'm marking this thread as incident triaged; we'll open a formal incident doc in #postmortems with timeline and action owners (Ana, Mike, Nina, Tariq). Closing after postmortem link posted. :white_check_mark:

Nina (oncall): Created incident ticket INC-2026-1732 and postmortem skeleton. Will ping when draft is ready.

SRE Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (temporary): dedicated-pool/eu-3 back under SLA thresholds.
